Frontier Research & Competitive Funding

Research Program

Investigating the neurocognitive architecture of human speech, language, and communication through multimodal Artificial Intelligence, neuroimaging, and computational linguistics—translating foundational brain science into scalable clinical biomarkers.

Frontier Research Vision: Decoding the Predictive Brain via Language Biomarkers

The Scientific Challenge: Neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental brain conditions alter the neural networks supporting speech and language years before overt clinical symptoms emerge. Yet gold-standard biological markers (CSF amyloid/tau, PET neuroimaging) remain invasive, costly, and inaccessible for population-scale screening, while traditional behavioral assessments are subjective, time-consuming, and language-specific.

Our High-Gain Approach: Human language production requires millisecond-level coordination across distributed cortical and subcortical networks. Our research program pioneers explainable, neurobiologically grounded, and cross-linguistically generalizable AI models that extract acoustic, prosodic, morphosyntactic, semantic, and information-theoretic footprints from natural connected speech and writing. By coupling computational linguistics and foundation models with structural/functional neuroimaging (fMRI, pCASL cerebral perfusion, DTI) and non-invasive brain stimulation (tDCS), we build transdiagnostic digital biomarkers that generalize across languages, dialects, and clinical populations.

5-Year Horizon Establish transdiagnostic, information-theoretic digital biomarkers quantifying predictive coding deficits and neuroplasticity across aphasia, MCI, Alzheimer’s disease, and neurodevelopmental disorders across diverse European languages via the Open Brain AI infrastructure.
10-Year Societal & Clinical Horizon Transform clinical neurology, speech-language pathology, and special needs education through ethical, transparent, and equitable AI diagnostics—enabling remote telehealth monitoring and personalized therapeutic interventions worldwide.

Four Core Research Pillars

Our research program integrates four synergistic areas spanning computational neurolinguistics, clinical AI, neuroimaging, and experimental phonetics.

Research Area 01

Automated Diagnosis, Prognosis & Therapy Efficacy via AI

Differential diagnosis and variant subtyping of Primary Progressive Aphasia (nfvPPA, svPPA, lvPPA), amnestic vs. non-amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), Alzheimer’s disease, and pediatric neurodevelopmental conditions (Autism Spectrum Disorder, DLD) require multidisciplinary expertise. We design deep neural networks, sequential architectures, and large language model embeddings that automate screening and variant classification from short spoken or written tasks.

Beyond diagnostics, we evaluate treatment efficacy in clinical trials combining behavioral language therapy with transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), quantifying subtle acoustic and phonological improvements in patients with apraxia of speech and aphasia.

Deep Neural Networks PPA & MCI Subtyping tDCS Neuromodulation Autism & DLD Screening

Research Area 02

Speech, Language & Neuroimaging Biomarkers

To ensure clinical AI models are biologically valid rather than opaque "black boxes," we map how structural atrophy, cerebral hypoperfusion, and disrupted functional connectivity alter human speech and language. Using Pseudo-Continuous Arterial Spin Labeling (pCASL) MRI, structural MRI, and Activation Likelihood Estimation (ALE) meta-analyses, we investigate how working memory, semantic, and prosodic brain networks support verbal learning and discourse.

In parallel, we identify novel behavioral biomarkers—including voice quality (cepstral peak prominence, harmonics-to-noise ratio), speech fluency, elaborative morphosyntax (function-to-content ratios, adjectives/adverbs), and information-theoretic surprisal/entropy metrics.

Research Area 03

Open Brain AI & Automated Clinical Tools

Manual transcription and clinical scoring of spoken discourse, spelling, and phonology are prohibitively labor-intensive and prone to inter-rater variability. We architect open-access computational platforms and validated distance-metric algorithms that automate clinical language assessment in seconds while matching gold-standard human raters ($r_s = .99$).

Our flagship platform, Open Brain AI, integrates multilingual speech-to-text, IPA phonemic conversion, morphosyntactic tagging, semantic/lexical profiling, and specialized clinical apps for spelling and phonological error analysis across 15+ languages.

Research Area 04

Speech Acoustics, Prosody & Sociolinguistic Variation

Speech signals simultaneously encode linguistic structure (phonemic category, stress, information structure, tonal alignment) and indexical/sociolinguistic identity (dialect, sociolect, L1/L2 background). Our experimental phonetics and sociophonetics research demonstrates that even brief sub-phonemic segments—such as stop consonant bursts, fricative spectra, and sonorant coarticulation—carry systematic dialectal signatures.

Understanding and modeling this acoustic gradience is vital for clinical speech-language pathology in bilectal, diglossic, and multilingual societies (such as Norway, Sweden, Greece, and Cyprus), preventing the misdiagnosis of dialectal or bilingual variation as speech pathology.
